name: Maftet — Additional Material (d20pfsrd)
body:
More on Maftet from d20pfsrd.com.

These sections appear on d20pfsrd.com's page "Maftet, Mythic" but are not part of the Maftet entry, which is unchanged.

hp 98 (8d10+54)
Fort +5, Ref +9, Will +8 Defensive Ability spell-storing tattoo (bestow curse)MMA; DR 5/epic

OFFENSE

Speed 40 ft., fly 60 ft. (poor)
Melee +1 scimitar +14/+14/+9/+9 (1d6+5/18-20)
Special Attacks mythic power (3/day, surge ++1d6), paired weapons, raptor dive, spinning divem, steal heartmma
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 8th; concentration +8)

Constant—mage armor
3/day—cure light wounds (DC 13), delay poison, magic missile, magic weapon

A mythic maftet can activate up to two of its spell-like abilities as a standard action. It may make a Fortitude save to resist the effects of an erase spell cast on its tattoos, but if it fails, it loses access to its spell-like abilities for 24 hours. Additionally, a mythic maftet has additional tattoos, beyond those available to its lesser kin. Each mythic maftet can select two additional 1st-level spells and one additional 2nd-level spell which it can use as spell-like abilities 3 times per day each, and one 3rd-level spell which it can use once per day. These spells are chosen from among the cleric and sorcerer/wizard spell lists. The example mythic maftet selected cure light wounds, delay poison, magic missile, and wind wall.

Spell-Storing Tattoo (Sp)

Mythic maftets have a special runic tattoo, in addition to the ones that allow them to perform spells. Each mythic maftet must choose a single spell of 4th-level or lower from the cleric or sorcerer/wizard spell list. If the chosen spell ever targets the mythic maftet, or the mythic maftet is included in its area, the spell is countered, as a counterspell action, requiring no action (or even knowledge) on the mythic maftet’s part. Each time this occurs, the mythic maftet gains the ability to cast that spell as a spell-like ability once. The mythic maftet can store up to three uses of the spell in this way, and as long as it has one or more uses of the spell available to it, its spell-storing tattoo glows faintly.

The example mythic maftet selected bestow curse.

Spinning Dive (Ex)

Whenever a mythic maftet uses its raptor dive ability, it can choose to expend a single use of mythic power in order to make it a spinning dive. If it does so, it gains a +2 dodge bonus to AC until the beginning of its next turn, the bonus to attack rolls granted by its raptor dive ability increases to +4, and the critical threat range of its falchions increases to 15-20 for the purposes of any attacks made as part of that action.

Steal Heart (Su)

As a full-round action, a maftet can plunge one hand into the chest of a helpless humanoid of Small or Medium size and rip out that creature’s still-beating heart. The creature must succeed on a Fortitude save (DC 18) or die instantly. If the creature succeeds on this saving throw, it suffers 8d10 points of piercing and slashing damage, but its heart is not removed. The creature’s heart continues to beat on its own after being removed, and the creature cannot be returned to life as long as the heart continues to beat. The heart can be consumed by any creature as a full-round action. Doing so consigns the soul of the creature whose heart is eaten to oblivion, preventing them from being resurrected by any means, unless a wish or miracle spell is used to restore their soul, but it also allows the creature that consumes the heart to absorb some of the creature’s knowledge. The creature that consumes the heart can learn one fact per 2 Hit Dice she possesses, based on the knowledge the creature whose heart was eaten possessed at the time that he died. This functions similarly to speak with dead, except that the creature’s body is not required (besides the heart) and the creature is not entitled to a Will save to resist the effect.

ECOLOGY

Environment temperate and warm deserts and mountains
Organization solitary, pair, or pride (1 mythic maftet and 7-12 nonmythic maftets)
Treasure standard (2 +1 scimitars, other treasure)
